advisories.title: Malware in @tekmidian/pai (npm): releases 1.0.8-1.0.10 carry malicious code
advisories.summary: Releases 1.0.8, 1.0.9 and 1.0.10 of @tekmidian/pai - a Personal AI Infrastructure / knowledge-OS package with federated memory and project management, run beside an agent that holds local project data - are malware (CWE-506, embedded malicious code). GitHub's advisory carries no patched version and no source to review; npm's latest tag is back at the clean 1.0.7. The advisory's standing advice: any computer that installed a poisoned release is fully compromised - rotate its secrets from a different machine, remove the package, and do not assume removing it cleans the machine.
advisories.affected: @tekmidian/pai 1.0.8, 1.0.9 and 1.0.10 (the releases the advisory lists). There is no patched build of those releases: 1.0.7 is the latest clean one, and the package should be removed.
patch: Remove the package (npm uninstall @tekmidian/pai; delete it from lockfiles and CI images), then treat the machine as compromised
Rotate every secret and key the machine held - from a different machine - and rebuild from a clean image; removing the package does not guarantee the machine is clean

advisories.title: Malware in @conduitops/logview-archive (npm): postinstall fetches and runs a payload from a disguised, masked registry URL
advisories.summary: Version 1.0.1 of @conduitops/logview-archive is a trojan. Its postinstall hook runs install.js, which shells out to 'npm install @conduit/logview-cli@2.2.0 --registry <decoded URL>', where the URL sits as a base64+XOR-masked string (key c0ndu1t-ops) in lib/toolchain.json and is decoded in memory by lib/origin.js. The decoded registry is a plain-HTTP bare IP - http://139.196.94.195:8080/dl/npm/ - not the public registry and nothing like the package's claimed conduit.internal provenance, so npm fetches and executes the lifecycle scripts of whatever package the attacker serves there: arbitrary install-time code execution on the installer's host. A comment in lib/origin.js says the masking is deliberate, leaving no readable address in the download. Reported by Amazon Inspector (IN-MAL-2026-021570) and published in the OSSF malicious-packages feed.
advisories.affected: @conduitops/logview-archive 1.0.1 (npm). There is no patched build: the package should be removed.
patch: Remove the package (npm uninstall @conduitops/logview-archive; delete it from lockfiles and CI images) and reinstall dependencies from the public registry
Treat the machine as compromised: rotate its secrets from a different machine and rebuild from a clean image
mitigation: Build hosts should not reach a plain-HTTP bare-IP registry: block 139.196.94.195 outbound, and pin npm to the public registry with an .npmrc scope check
iocs: 139.196.94.195:8080 (the masked registry the postinstall fetches from)

advisories.title: Linux KSMBD (in-kernel SMB server): two unpatched remote code execution bugs, one before login (ZDI-CAN-33774, ZDI-CAN-33549)
advisories.summary: Trend Micro's ZDI sent two CVSS 9.0 KSMBD reports to public kernel mailing lists before any fix existed. ZDI-CAN-33774: a race in protocol dispatch (a burst of short SMB1 packets followed by an SMB2 packet in one TCP write) makes the server read past a buffer with no authentication, over TCP 445; with access to a share it can also write past it. ZDI-CAN-33549: an integer underflow in the SMB Direct (RDMA) path overruns a buffer; it needs an RDMA-capable interface (or the rxe software driver), a writable share and a client negotiating SMB Direct. No fix in mainline, linux-next or stable yet, so no CVE. Samba (smbd) is separate software and is not affected.
advisories.affected: Linux machines running KSMBD (the ksmbd kernel module loaded, started by ksmbd-tools / ksmbd.service), above all with TCP 445 reachable from untrusted networks. A kernel that merely ships the module, unloaded, is not exposed; Samba is not affected.
patch: No kernel fix exists yet: when your distro ships a kernel that names ZDI-CAN-33774 / ZDI-CAN-33549 (or their CVEs), install it and reboot
mitigation: Not using KSMBD: stop it and keep it from loading: systemctl disable --now ksmbd; rmmod ksmbd; echo 'install ksmbd /bin/false' > /etc/modprobe.d/disable-ksmbd.conf
Need the share: allow TCP 445 only from trusted hosts at the firewall, never from the internet
SMB Direct (ZDI-CAN-33549): do not load rdma_rxe or offer SMB Direct on the share host until it is patched

advisories.title: Next.js 16.0.0-16.4.0: unauthenticated RCE in `use cache` functions returning typed arrays
advisories.summary: An application using the App Router with Cache Components can be driven to remote code execution through a use cache function that returns multiple typed arrays. No authentication is needed, and Vercel publishes no workaround for applications that have such functions: upgrade immediately even if yours does not look like the shape they name. This is the third Next.js advisory in this feed this week, after the Image Optimization RCE and the Server Actions DoS (nextjs-2026-10); 16.4.1 carries all three fixes.
advisories.affected: next 16.0.0 up to 16.4.0, when the app uses App Router with Cache Components and has a use cache function returning multiple typed arrays.
patch: npm install next@^16.4.1, rebuild and redeploy
mitigation: No workaround is published for affected applications - upgrading is the only fix, and Vercel says to do it even when you think you have no such function
While planning the upgrade, audit use cache functions that return multiple typed arrays

advisories.title: DOMPurify before 3.4.17: SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES bypass through shadow root content, and armed handlers in hook-detached subtrees
advisories.summary: Two sanitization gaps closed in one release. With SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES and a DOM-returning mode (RETURN_DOM, RETURN_DOM_FRAGMENT or IN_PLACE), template expressions like {{...}}, ${...} and <%...%> split across text nodes inside an attached shadow root survive sanitization: DOMPurify's final normalize-and-re-scrub pass never descends into shadow trees (per DOM spec, neither normalize() nor NodeIterator does), so once the disallowed elements between the fragments are removed they join into an expression a downstream template engine evaluates - cross-site scripting client-side, template injection server-side. Second: in IN_PLACE mode a hook that removes a node other than itself - its parent or a later sibling - leaves that detached subtree unvisited and un-neutralized, so event handlers on it stay armed and an img onerror already loading fires after sanitize() returns (an incomplete fix for GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p).
advisories.affected: dompurify up to 3.4.16. The shadow-root bypass needs SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES together with RETURN_DOM, RETURN_DOM_FRAGMENT or IN_PLACE and attacker-influenced DOM nodes carrying an attached shadow root (3.4.4+); the handler gap needs IN_PLACE with hooks that remove a parent or sibling (tested on 2.5.8 through 3.4.16).
patch: npm install dompurify@^3.4.17 and rebuild
mitigation: Until upgraded: do not feed DOM nodes with shadow roots into a SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES configuration
Do not trust an IN_PLACE hook that removes a parent or sibling to neutralize what it detached - scrub that subtree yourself before removing it

advisories.title: GitPython before 3.2.1: create_submodule clones into .git/hooks before the path check, planting a git hook (RCE)
advisories.summary: create_submodule(name, path, url) clones the submodule before it rejects the destination path. A path of .git/hooks passes the pre-clone check, so the clone lands in the repository's live hooks directory and a file named post-checkout in the submodule becomes an executable .git/hooks/post-checkout - code execution at the next git operation. On 3.2.0 the later index check does raise, but only after the clone wrote to disk and without removing the planted hook; on 3.1.x nothing checks and the call succeeds silently. Reachable wherever an application hands an attacker-influenced path or URL to Submodule.add()/create_submodule() - repo tooling, web UIs that add submodules, CI utilities.
advisories.affected: GitPython 3.1.x and 3.2.0 (fixed in 3.2.1).
patch: pip install --upgrade 'GitPython>=3.2.1' wherever submodules are added through it, then restart the services using it
mitigation: Until upgraded: never pass an untrusted path or URL to Submodule.add()/create_submodule(); add submodules through the git CLI after reviewing the path
iocs: a git hook you did not write appearing under .git/hooks of a repository this library manages

advisories.title: toml (toml-node) before 5.0.1: parsing a crafted TOML document writes to Object.prototype
advisories.summary: The 4.1.2 fix for CVE-2026-63376 is bypassable: the path-key encoding is still ambiguous (a quote plays the dot's role, and a quote inside a segment is never escaped), a table-array header can clear another key's guard bookkeeping, and the assign() descent has no owned-container check - a TOML datetime is a Date object whose prototype chain reaches Object.prototype. A four-line TOML document parsed with toml.parse() writes a property onto Object.prototype where every object in the process sees it, including objects from unrelated libraries - the classic prototype pollution foothold. (The npm package is toml; the advisory record lists it as tome.)
advisories.affected: toml up to 5.0.0 (npm package toml, the BinaryMuse/toml-node parser).
patch: npm install toml@^5.0.1 wherever TOML is parsed with toml.parse(), then restart
mitigation: Until upgraded: do not parse TOML from untrusted sources with this package - JSON or a validated parser avoids the whole class

advisories.title: @graphql-tools/utils before 12.0.2: prototype pollution in mergeIncrementalResult via non-primitive path segments
advisories.summary: mergeIncrementalResult merges an incremental GraphQL response part into the accumulated result by walking ['data', ...path] and writing at the resolved location. setObjectKeyPath blocks __proto__, constructor and prototype by strict string equality but never checks that a path segment is a primitive string or number, so a segment like a ['__proto__'] array slips past the guard and lands a write on Object.prototype. No options are involved: the vulnerable path is on by default. An attacker who influences an incremental (defer/stream) response can pollute the prototype of a GraphQL server or client process.
advisories.affected: @graphql-tools/utils 10.10.1 up to 12.0.1 (10.10.0 and older do not carry the vulnerable code). The fix ships only on the 12.x line.
patch: npm install @graphql-tools/utils@^12.0.2 - a major bump from 10.x/11.x; move the other @graphql-tools/* packages with it - then rebuild and redeploy
mitigation: Until upgraded: do not merge incremental GraphQL results from untrusted subgraphs or executors; validate that response paths contain only strings before incremental merging

advisories.title: nbconvert before 7.17.2: arbitrary file write through cell output filenames (path traversal when exporting)
advisories.summary: ExtractOutputPreprocessor joins an attacker-controlled filename attribute from ipynb cell output metadata onto output_files_dir with no canonicalization check, so converting a malicious notebook writes attacker-chosen data to attacker-chosen paths - the report's example overwrites targets reached through ../ traversal, such as authorized_keys. Vulnerable exports: --to markdown, latex, rst and asciidoc. A sibling of GHSA-4c99-qj7h-p3vg. Any service, CI job or doc pipeline that converts notebooks it did not author is the exposure; running the cells in Jupyter first would overwrite the malicious output and hide it.
advisories.affected: nbconvert 5.4.0 up to 7.17.1.
patch: pip install --upgrade 'nbconvert>=7.17.2' on every host that converts notebooks (Jupyter servers, CI images, doc pipelines)
mitigation: Until upgraded: do not run nbconvert on .ipynb files you did not author; strip output metadata (the filename attributes) from untrusted notebooks before converting

advisories.title: Black before 26.10.1: its GitHub Action installs an unvalidated required-version from pyproject.toml (RCE via pull request)
advisories.summary: The GitHub Action bundled with Black reads tool.black.required-version from pyproject.toml when use_pyproject is true and installs that value as the Black version without validating it, so a pull request that edits pyproject.toml can point the action at a malicious repository and run its code in the context of the victim's repository - the same class as CVE-2026-31900. Anyone running psf/black's action with use_pyproject: true on pull_request events is exposed, and the attacker only needs to open a PR.
advisories.affected: The bundled GitHub Action in Black releases before 26.10.1, in workflows that set use_pyproject: true.
patch: In every workflow using psf/black's action, pin it to 26.10.1 or newer (uses: psf/black@26.10.1 or a tag you verified); pip install --upgrade 'black>=26.10.1' where Black is used from PyPI
mitigation: Until the action pin is fixed: stop setting use_pyproject: true (then the required-version path is not read), or require approval for pull_request runs from forks and protect pyproject.toml with CODEOWNERS

advisories.title: Django REST framework before 3.18.2: silent no-op token revocation, an Accept-header CPU denial of service, and request-stream codec injection
advisories.summary: Three bugs, one upgrade. TokenProxy.delete() reports success and revokes nothing: its pk returns the user id and Model.delete() matches that against the 40-character key column, so every caller that revokes a token through TokenProxy - anything outside the shipped admin, which re-fetches the concrete row - believes a live credential is gone (CVE-2026-114137). A crafted Accept header of many large quoted parameters burns about 19 seconds of CPU per unauthenticated request in content negotiation; two concurrent requests stop a default two-worker deployment answering (CVE-2026-114138). And JSONParser applies an attacker-named codec from the Content-Type charset parameter to the request stream: charset=bz2_codec turns a 108-byte body into a 50-million-character value inside the view, defeating DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE and ballooning worker memory (CVE-2026-114136).
advisories.affected: djangorestframework up to 3.18.1: the codec injection from 3.6.4, TokenProxy.delete() from 3.12.0, the Accept-header DoS per the record in all of < 3.18.2. The shipped TokenAdmin path is not affected by the revocation bug.
patch: pip install --upgrade 'djangorestframework>=3.18.2', then restart the app workers
mitigation: Until upgraded: revoke tokens through the concrete model (Token.objects.get(key=...).delete()), never TokenProxy.delete(), and re-check anything your scripts believe they revoked since 3.12.0
Cap request header sizes at the proxy and reject Content-Type charset values that are not plain text codecs
Rotate any token whose revocation you cannot prove

advisories.title: Malware in opencode-skills-collection (npm): agent skill collection releases carry malicious code
advisories.summary: Releases of the opencode-skills-collection npm package - an OpenCode CLI plugin that downloads and keeps agent skills up to date - are malware (CWE-506, embedded malicious code). GitHub's advisory carries no patched version and no source to review. Agent-skill packages run with the privileges of the agent that loads them, which on a developer or CI machine means the keys in its environment: the poisoned releases sit in the 4.0.56-4.1.20 range the advisory lists, and the advisory's standing advice is that any computer that installed the package is fully compromised.
advisories.affected: opencode-skills-collection 4.0.56, 4.0.57, 4.0.77 and 4.1.0 through 4.1.20 (the releases the advisory lists). There is no clean upgrade: the package should be removed.
patch: Remove the package (npm uninstall opencode-skills-collection; delete it from lockfiles and CI images)
Treat the machine as compromised: rotate every secret and key it held, from a different machine, and rebuild from a clean image - removing the package does not guarantee the machine is clean

advisories.title: Malware in agentic-awesome-skills (npm): agent skill collection releases carry malicious code
advisories.summary: Releases of the agentic-awesome-skills npm package - AAS Core, a local collection of 2700+ agentic skills that agents discover and load - are malware (CWE-506, embedded malicious code), with no patched version and no source to review. A skill collection runs with the privileges of the agent that loads it: on a developer or CI machine that is the whole key environment. The advisory lists the poisoned releases across 18.9.0-18.14.0 and 19.0.0-19.13.0, and its standing advice is that any computer that installed the package is fully compromised.
advisories.affected: agentic-awesome-skills 18.9.0 through 18.14.0 and 19.0.0 through 19.13.0 (the releases the advisory lists). There is no clean upgrade: the package should be removed.
patch: Remove the package (npm uninstall agentic-awesome-skills; delete it from lockfiles and CI images)
Treat the machine as compromised: rotate every secret and key it held, from a different machine, and rebuild from a clean image - removing the package does not guarantee the machine is clean

advisories.title: Next.js before 15.5.28 / 16.4.1: unauthenticated RCE through Image Optimization with SVG, and a Server Actions denial of service
advisories.summary: Two bugs, one upgrade. The Image Optimization API can be made to trigger a use-after-free in librsvg while processing an SVG through sharp, and when Next.js runs on glibc-based Linux that memory bug is exploitable for unauthenticated remote code execution (CVE-2026-96889, the librsvg bug listed separately in this feed as librsvg-xinclude-uaf). Separately, crafted requests to an App Router application with at least one Server Action drive CPU usage until the process stops answering other requests (CVE-2026-94482). Upgrading Next.js moves sharp to a build that carries the fixed librsvg.
advisories.affected: next 10.0.0 up to 15.5.27 and 16.0.0 up to 16.4.0 for the RCE (needs the Image Optimization API processing SVG files, Next.js on a glibc Linux); next 13.0.0 up to 15.5.27 and 16.0.0 up to 16.4.0 for the DoS (needs App Router with at least one Server Action; Pages Router apps and apps without Server Actions are not hit). sharp below 0.35.5 carries the vulnerable librsvg.
patch: npm install next@^15.5.28 or next@^16.4.1 (or your framework's pinned upgrade), rebuild and redeploy; a fresh install pulls a sharp with the fixed librsvg
Docker: rebuild the image so the new sharp/librsvg lands, then redeploy
mitigation: Until upgraded: keep the Image Optimization API from processing SVGs - do not allow SVG sources into the optimizer
Or ensure the sharp Next.js uses is 0.35.5 or newer (the vendor's own workaround); check npm ls sharp
For the DoS: rate-limit or block unauthenticated POSTs to Server Action endpoints at the proxy until upgraded

advisories.title: Librsvg before 2.57.5 / 2.60.3 / 2.61.5 / 2.62.4 / 2.63.2: use-after-free rendering an SVG whose XML includes declare a duplicated entity (CVE-2026-96889)
advisories.summary: Librsvg parses XML with libxml2. In an SVG with a nested XInclude, an XML entity declaration whose name duplicates one already in use makes the included parse free an xmlEntity that the outer parse keeps using - a use-after-free over a freed 144-byte node that a crafted SVG triggers in whatever renders it. Hosts that render untrusted SVGs are exposed (rsvg-convert, thumbnailers, media pipelines, image proxies); through sharp the same bug also reaches Next.js Image Optimization, where it is unauthenticated RCE on glibc Linux (see nextjs-2026-10). The fix stops freeing xmlEntity pointers libxml2 still uses. Red Hat has shipped errata; the GNOME work item is 1241.
advisories.affected: librsvg up to 2.57.4, 2.60.0-beta up to 2.60.2, 2.61.0 up to 2.61.4, 2.62.0-beta up to 2.62.3, 2.63.0-beta up to 2.63.1. Distro builds may carry the fix under an older number (the changelog check below reads that).
patch: Debian/Ubuntu: apt update && apt install librsvg2-common librsvg2-bin librsvg2-2 (the distro's fixed or backported build); Fedora/RHEL: dnf update librsvg2 librsvg2-tools
Rebuild containers and image pipelines that bundle librsvg, and any sharp below 0.35.5, then redeploy
mitigation: Until updated: do not render untrusted SVGs with librsvg - reject SVG uploads at the edge or convert them with a renderer outside librsvg
The bug is in XML includes: stripping xi:include elements and entity declarations from incoming SVGs removes the trigger

advisories.title: PyJWT before 2.14.0: HS256/384/512 verification accepts an empty HMAC key from an oct JWK, so a forged token passes (PyJWK / PyJWKClient)
advisories.summary: HMACAlgorithm.from_jwk accepts a symmetric JWK (kty=oct) whose k value is the empty string and returns a zero-length key without raising. Verifying a token with that key object - a PyJWK, or one built by PyJWKSet or PyJWKClient from a JWKS - computes the HMAC with an empty key, so any token an attacker forged with the same empty key verifies: no secret knowledge needed, just reproduce the digest with key b"" and set the token's kid to the empty-key JWK. The empty-key rejection that prepare_key gained in 2.13.0 for string and bytes secrets never reached the from_jwk path, and by default a short key only warns (InsecureKeyLengthWarning) instead of failing. The same empty-HMAC-key defect is being closed across the JWT ecosystem (fast-jwt CVE-2026-44351).
advisories.affected: PyJWT up to 2.13.0 where verification uses JWK or JWKS keys (PyJWK, PyJWKSet, PyJWKClient) with HMAC algorithms HS256/384/512. Applications that pass a plain string or bytes secret to jwt.decode are not affected: that path has rejected empty keys since 2.13.0.
patch: pip install --upgrade 'PyJWT>=2.14.0' everywhere tokens are verified, then restart the app workers
mitigation: Until upgraded: verify with enforce_minimum_key_length so a short key raises instead of warning, or reject oct JWKs with an empty or short k when you load JWKS
Prefer passing the HMAC secret as a string or bytes key (that path has rejected empty keys since 2.13.0) over JWK objects
Rotate signing keys if untrusted JWKS input could reach the verifier

advisories.title: Jupyter Server 2.0.0-2.5.0: gateway WebSocket handler skips the kernel execute authorization check (CVE-2026-114135)
advisories.summary: When GatewayClient.url is configured, Jupyter Server replaces the normal kernel channel handler with a gateway-specific one. That handler checks only that the caller is authenticated and never asks the configured Authorizer whether the user may execute on kernels, so an authenticated user who is deliberately denied execute - a read-only or otherwise limited account - can still open a kernel channel and send messages to the upstream kernel, obtaining kernel execution with whatever data and credentials that kernel holds. A missing authorization check, not an authentication bypass: it matters in deployments that use a restrictive custom Authorizer together with Jupyter Gateway or Enterprise Gateway. The 2.6.0 fix routes gateway traffic through GatewayWebSocketConnection instead of replacing the handler; the deprecated handler is still present and must not be registered by hand.
advisories.affected: jupyter-server 2.0.0 up to 2.5.0 with GatewayClient.url set (Jupyter Gateway / Enterprise Gateway deployments).
patch: pip install --upgrade 'jupyter-server>=2.6.0' (or your JupyterLab / Hub distribution's equivalent), then restart the jupyter server or gateway
mitigation: Until upgraded: do not register the deprecated gateway WebSocketChannelsHandler yourself, and keep execute-denied users off the gateway's kernel routes at the proxy (authentication is checked, execute rights are not)
Audit the Authorizer: the gap only matters where authorization is stricter than 'any authenticated user may execute'

advisories.title: Sentry-Javascript before 9.47.2 / 10.75.2 / 11.0.0-rc.1: the Next.js tunnel route skips middleware on more than the tunnel path (CVE-2026-114139)
advisories.summary: With tunnelRoute set, the Sentry Next.js SDK sends browser events to a path on your own Next.js server and skips middleware for those envelope requests so the tunnel rewrite can pass them on. The skip was wider than the rewrite: the rewrite only serves the tunnel path itself, but the skip covered everything under it, so a request in that gap - /monitoring/foo for a /monitoring tunnel, or anything a dynamic app/[locale]/ segment matches - reaches your application with middleware never running. Skipping middleware grants no privileges of its own: routes that check the session server-side stay protected. Sentry itself rates the issue Moderate (the setup it needs is narrow); the advisory database rates it critical.
advisories.affected: @sentry/nextjs 9.36.0 up to 9.47.1, 10.x up to 10.75.1 and 11.0.0 pre-releases up to 11.0.0-rc.0, and only where all of these hold: tunnelRoute is set, the app is built with webpack (Turbopack builds are not affected), some route resolves under the tunnel path, and middleware is the only place that enforces authorization for that route. Sentry's own services and organization data are not affected.
patch: npm install @sentry/nextjs@^9.47.2 (or ^10.75.2, or the 11.0.0-rc.1 pre-release) and rebuild; no configuration change is needed
mitigation: Until upgraded: set tunnelRoute to a path no route of yours can resolve under, or remove the option
Build with Turbopack (the default for next build from Next.js 16), which is not affected
Enforce authorization in the route, layout or data-access path as well as in middleware

advisories.title: virtualenv before 21.14.9: generated activate scripts and pip launchers run commands from an attacker-named path
advisories.summary: virtualenv writes the environment's directory name and path into every script it generates, and five bugs let that text run as shell code. The attacker's input is a directory name: a cloned repository, an unpacked archive, or a CI path built from a branch or job name. In bash, activate escapes the name for only one of bash's two PS1 passes, so a name like a\$(touch pwned) runs at every prompt; under zsh with PROMPT_SUBST on (oh-my-zsh's default) the raw name is expanded the same way; activate.fish quotes with POSIX sh rules that fish reads differently, so a backslash before a quote escapes out of the literal; a path containing a placeholder name such as __VIRTUAL_NAME__ is rewritten after quoting and breaks out into code; and the POSIX console launchers (bin/pip and friends) hand the interpreter path to distlib's #!/bin/sh wrapper unescaped, which expands the payload when the user runs the launcher. Nothing runs when the environment is created - the user must source activate or run a generated script from an environment an attacker named. Per bug: launchers CVE-2026-113722 (21.14.8 only, fixed 21.14.9), bash PS1 CVE-2026-113725 (up to 21.14.6, fixed 21.14.7), zsh PROMPT_SUBST CVE-2026-113726 (up to 21.14.3, fixed 21.14.4), fish quoting CVE-2026-113732 (up to 21.14.1, fixed 21.14.2), placeholder rewrite CVE-2026-113776 (20.26.6-21.14.1, fixed 21.14.2).
advisories.affected: virtualenv up to 21.14.8, per vector: console launchers 21.14.8, bash activate up to 21.14.6, zsh up to 21.14.3, activate.fish and the template rewrite up to 21.14.1 (the rewrite bug only since 20.26.6). Windows exe launchers are not affected. A dev-machine and CI bug: build hosts that create environments under paths named after a branch, project or job are the exposure.

checks.label: virtualenv
command: virtualenv --version 2>/dev/null || python3 -c "import importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version('virtualenv'))"

patch: pip install --upgrade 'virtualenv>=21.14.9' wherever environments are created (pipx upgrade virtualenv, your distro package, or the CI image)
Recreate environments whose path or prompt was not fully trusted: the generated activate and launcher scripts carry the bug and upgrading virtualenv does not rewrite them
mitigation: Do not create an environment under a path someone else named: check a cloned repository's or unpacked archive's directory names before running virtualenv there

VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1 before sourcing activate (bash, zsh), or shopt -u promptvars (bash) / unsetopt prompt_subst (zsh) when the prompt needs no expansion; inspect activate.fish and the bin/ scripts before running one you did not create
pip's vendored distlib can write the vulnerable launcher wrapper again on a later pip install or upgrade inside an environment - the virtualenv fix does not patch pip's copy, so keep pip current

advisories.title: OpenChoreo before 1.0.6 / 1.1.7 / 1.2.5: WorkflowRun update authorization bypass lets one project take over another's runs
advisories.summary: The OpenChoreo API server authorized PUT .../workflowruns/{runName} against the openchoreo.dev/project and openchoreo.dev/component labels supplied in the request body, while the run it mutated is the one named in the URL. A caller holding workflowrun:update on one component could name a run of another project or component in the URL, send their own labels, pass the check, and rewrite the victim run's ownership labels. Every other WorkflowRun permission - view, logs, events, status, delete - derives from those stored labels, so after the write the attacker legitimately reads the victim's build logs (raw pod logs that routinely carry source paths, registry destinations and credentials a build step echoed), deletes the run, or overwrites a pending run's parameters. Needs an authenticated caller with an AuthzRoleBinding or ClusterAuthzRoleBinding for workflowrun:update in the same namespace plus the run's name; anonymous callers cannot reach it; cross-project and cross-component inside one namespace, not cross-tenant.
patch: Upgrade to the patched release on your line: 1.0.6, 1.1.7 or 1.2.5; no configuration change is needed after upgrading (the fix also makes the two ownership labels immutable on update)
mitigation: Until upgraded: restrict who holds workflowrun:update - audit AuthzRole and ClusterAuthzRole definitions for that action and drop it from any role held by principals you would not trust with write access to every workflow run in the namespace

Among the shipped roles only workload-publisher lists workflowrun:update (admin holds it through its * wildcard), and custom roles in your own values file may too: treat any credential bound to workload-publisher, typically a CI token, as privileged

advisories.title: ApostropheCMS before 4.33.0: unauthenticated big-upload processing drains the server (@apostrophecms/import-export)
advisories.summary: The chunked import routes (importExportImport on pages and piece types) run bigUploadMiddleware() before the import handler's own req.user check and pass it no authorize callback, so an unauthenticated request drives the whole aposBigUpload start / chunk / end flow first: the server creates upload state, writes attacker chunk data into big-uploads, processes temporary files, and loops cleanup over an attacker-declared chunk count - only then does the import handler reject the caller. An anonymous remote attacker burns storage, filesystem I/O and CPU at will (CWE-400 denial of service) and gets arbitrary file content written to the server before any authentication. Reported by Kai Zhi; no exploitation known.
advisories.affected: @apostrophecms/import-export 3.6.2 (confirmed) and likely earlier 3.x with the big-upload import implementation, paired with apostrophe up to 4.32.x.
patch: npm install apostrophe@^4.33.0 @apostrophecms/import-export@^3.7.0 (or update package.json and reinstall), then restart the app
mitigation: Until upgraded: block unauthenticated POSTs to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/*/importExportImport at the reverse proxy, or remove @apostrophecms/import-export if nobody imports
Watch the big-uploads and temp directories for growth you did not cause and clean up orphaned chunk files

advisories.title: Pillow before 13.0.0: Ghostscript argument injection to RCE, and a heap overflow saving TIFF
advisories.summary: Two critical bugs in Python's image library. When the file name passed to Image.open() for an EPS is attacker-influenced (an upload stored under its own name), Pillow hands it to Ghostscript unchecked: a leading - or @ injects Ghostscript arguments, verified to run commands even with -dSAFER. Re-saving an uploaded image as TIFF to an in-memory target (BytesIO, an HTTP response, a storage stream) overflows the heap and copies stale heap bytes into the output. 13.0.0 also fixes about a dozen high-severity crash and memory bugs published the same day.
advisories.affected: Pillow 2.0.0 up to 13.0.0 (TIFF save to a non-file target), Pillow 2.6.0 up to 13.0.0 (EPS via Ghostscript, needs Ghostscript installed). Saves to real file paths are not affected by the TIFF bug.
patch: pip install --upgrade 'Pillow>=13.0.0' in every virtualenv that handles user images (pin it in requirements / lock files), then restart the app workers
Docker: rebuild images with Pillow 13.0.0 or newer and redeploy
mitigation: Until upgraded: never pass a user-chosen file name to Image.open(); store uploads under generated names or open them from a file object
Where EPS is not needed, keep it from reaching Ghostscript (Image.open(f, formats=[...]) with only the formats you accept, or no Ghostscript on the host)
Save TIFFs to a real file path, not io.BytesIO or a stream

advisories.title: Storybook dev server: a malicious website can change project files (CVE-2026-114125)
advisories.summary: While storybook dev runs, a website open in the developer's browser can reach the dev server on localhost and change files in the project; under further conditions a changed file is then run with the developer's privileges. Built Storybooks, and dev servers never opened in a browser (headless automation, MCP clients), are not affected. Storybook knows of no exploitation.
advisories.affected: storybook (and @storybook/core, @storybook/core-server, @storybook/experimental-addon-test, @storybook/addon-vitest, @storybook/addon-mcp) 8.0.0 before 8.6.19, 9.x before 9.1.21, 10.x before 10.6.2, 11.0.0-alpha before 11.0.0-alpha.6.
patch: Upgrade storybook and every @storybook/* package to 10.6.2 (9.1.21 on 9.x, 8.6.19 on 8.x, 11.0.0-alpha.6 on the 11 alpha) and commit the lockfile before running storybook dev again
Read the advisory's list of changed network defaults: the fix changes how the dev server accepts connections, also on 8.x and 9.x
mitigation: Do not run an affected storybook dev server until it is upgraded
Deny the browser's permission prompt for a website to connect to localhost unless you trust the site
iocs: Project file changes you did not make while storybook dev was running (git status / git diff)

advisories.title: PHP2Shell: unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP core
advisories.summary: Two memory-corruption bugs in PHP's session upload-progress path (on by default since PHP 5.4) let one request run code on the server before any application code runs. WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and MediaWiki are all reachable. Details leaked before the fix; exploit attempts started the same day.
advisories.affected: PHP 8.5 before 8.5.12, 8.4 before 8.4.27, 8.3 before 8.3.36, 8.2 before 8.2.35, and every end-of-life line (8.1 and older), under every SAPI (FPM, mod_php, CGI, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed).
patch: Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt update && sudo apt install --only-upgrade 'php*' then sudo systemctl restart 'php*-fpm' apache2 (whichever you run)
RHEL/Alma/Rocky/Fedora: sudo dnf upgrade 'php*' then restart php-fpm / httpd
Docker: rebuild on php:8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35 (or newer) base images and redeploy
Source builds: upgrade to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35; PHP 7.4/8.0/8.1 have source backports only (php.net), so move to 8.2+
Managed hosting: confirm with the host that PHP was updated and workers restarted
mitigation: Until patched: session.upload_progress.enabled = 0 in php.ini or the FPM pool (not ini_set or .user.ini), then restart every PHP worker
PHP 8.5: fatal_error_backtraces = 0
post_max_size 8M (32M if you take uploads) with upload_max_filesize below it
These only narrow the attack; only the update fixes it
iocs: Unexpected child processes of php-fpm/apache (shells, curl, wget): watch with https://github.com/Neo23x0/process-watcher

advisories.title: Node.js October security release: Brotli decoder RCE and 9 more
advisories.summary: An out-of-bounds write in Node's Brotli decoder can run code when a server decompresses attacker data; the same release fixes TLS hostname-check bypasses and a dns.resolve truncation, and drops the eMudhra CA from Node's bundled store.
advisories.affected: Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x before the fixed releases, and every end-of-life line.
patch: nvm: nvm install 24.22.1 (or 22.23.4 / 26.12.1) && nvm alias default 24.22.1
Debian/Ubuntu (NodeSource): sudo apt update && sudo apt install --only-upgrade nodejs
Docker: rebuild on node:22.23.4 / 24.22.1 / 26.12.1 (or newer) and redeploy
Restart every Node process after upgrading
mitigation: Until patched: refuse Content-Encoding: br request bodies at the reverse proxy and do not decompress untrusted Brotli in app code (Vercel's WAF already blocks known patterns for Vercel deployments)

advisories.title: GitLab: unauthenticated RCE through the regex compiler (CVSS 10)
advisories.summary: An integer overflow in GitLab's regex compiler lets anyone reach code execution on a self-managed server; it spans 12 years of releases. The same fixed releases supersede the October 12 fix for CVE-2026-97229 (CI/CD regex RCE, also CVSS 10). GitLab.com and Dedicated are already patched.
advisories.affected: GitLab CE/EE self-managed 7.0 up to 18.11.12, 19.0 before 19.0.10, 19.1 before 19.1.9, 19.2 before 19.2.9, 19.3 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, 19.5 before 19.5.1.
patch: Omnibus (Debian/Ubuntu): sudo apt update && sudo apt install gitlab-ee (or gitlab-ce) to 19.5.1 or the fixed patch of your minor
Omnibus (RHEL): sudo dnf upgrade gitlab-ee (or gitlab-ce)
Docker: pull gitlab/gitlab-ee:19.5.1-ee.0 (or your minor's fixed tag) and recreate the container
Then: sudo gitlab-ctl reconfigure && sudo gitlab-ctl restart
mitigation: None published; take the instance off the public internet until upgraded
iocs: GitLab published detections for CVE-2026-97229 (e.g. Onigmo native worker crashes) in its 19.4.2 release post

advisories.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway before 14.1-73.41 / 13.1-64.28: memory overflow in SAML auth, exploited to reboot internet-facing appliances (CVE-2026-88779)
advisories.summary: A memory buffer overflow in NetScaler's SAML authentication path (CWE-119, CVSS v4 8.7) crashes the appliance; triggered repeatedly the service stays down. Citrix says it has observed targeted attacks on unmitigated deployments and rates the impact availability-only, but the field reports are nastier: administrators saw crafted SAML usernames carrying shell commands that tried to download and run a payload from 213.209.159[.]55, patched appliances rebooted in loops, Kevin Beaumont found a honeypot running a downloaded binary, and watchTowr reproduced the flaw. CISA's KEV catalog added it on October 4, the day Citrix published the bulletin and emergency builds, with a federal deadline of October 7; attempts seen so far look like broad spraying. Applies to appliances configured as a SAML service provider or SAML identity provider; Secure Private Access Hybrid deployments on NetScaler instances are affected too. Appliances already updated for the earlier NetScaler flaws (CVE-2026-88771 through 88778) need this upgrade as well. This entry carries the October 4 date because the feed's scan window missed it then; it is still exploited and still unpatched on many appliances.
advisories.affected: NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-73.41, 13.1 before 13.1-64.28, ADC FIPS before 14.1-73.41 FIPS, and ADC FIPS/NDcPP before 13.1-37.282 - when configured with SAML authentication on a Gateway or AAA virtual server (an 'add authentication samlAction' or 'add authentication samlIdPProfile' entry in the running config).
patch: Upgrade to 14.1-73.41 (FIPS: 14.1-73.41 FIPS; 13.1 line: 13.1-64.28; ADC FIPS/NDcPP on 13.1: 13.1-37.282) from Citrix's downloads, then reboot the appliance
Secure Private Access Hybrid: upgrade the NetScaler instances as well; Citrix-managed cloud services are already updated
mitigation: Until upgraded: enable Citrix's Global Deny List signatures (NetScaler Console 'Virtual patching' on; default-on from 14.1-60.52 and 13.1-63.21; check 'show appfw signatures' shows Encrypted Version at least v24)
Restrict management and SAML endpoints where the topology allows (ACLs on the management interface), and review logs for repeated reboots, nsaaad crashes and unexpected files
No SAML action configured means the vendor's precondition is absent - confirm before you deprioritize the upgrade
iocs: 213.209.159.55 (payload host seen in crafted SAML usernames)

advisories.title: GitLab: unauthenticated arbitrary file read (CVSS 10), exploited
advisories.summary: A path traversal in the commits API reads any file on the server with one request: CI/CD secrets, deploy tokens, SSH keys. In CISA's exploited list since September 11 and still being hit (reposted widely on October 21).
advisories.affected: GitLab CE/EE 18.7 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, 19.3 before 19.3.2. An 18.x instance should move to a current 19.x release.
patch: Upgrade as for gitlab-110264 (its fixed releases include this fix)
Then rotate CI/CD variables, deploy tokens, runner tokens and SSH keys, and hunt for unknown access
mitigation: None; upgrade

advisories.title: Drupal core: remote code execution in Field UI (SA-CORE-2026-014)
advisories.summary: A remote code execution bug in Drupal core's Field UI, reachable through contributed modules or custom code. Drupal sites also run on PHP, so patch php2shell too.
advisories.affected: Drupal core before 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19.
patch: composer update 'drupal/core-*' --with-all-dependencies, then drush updatedb && drush cache:rebuild

advisories.title: WordPress: Rank Math SEO PRO 3.0.123 shipped a backdoor
advisories.summary: The PRO build downloaded between Oct 15 20:02 and Oct 16 07:12 UTC carried a self-rebuilding backdoor. Updating alone is not enough once it was active: it re-plants itself.
advisories.affected: Rank Math PRO 3.0.123, if it was activated. The free wordpress.org plugin is not affected.
patch: Best: restore files and database from a backup taken before 2026-10-15 20:02 UTC, then install 3.0.124

Otherwise, in order: delete the whole Rank Math PRO plugin folder; delete wp_options rows _uf6qdn2hmm, t8krdk990phb, _np5pvf754c; block rank1cdn.com; check mu-plugins, fake core files, PHP under .cache, cron entries and unknown admins; reinstall 3.0.124
Then rotate WordPress passwords, DB credentials, salts, and API/payment/SMTP/hosting/SSH keys

advisories.title: WordPress: stolen UpdraftCentral keys used to take over sites
advisories.summary: teamupdraft.com was breached; stolen UpdraftCentral cloud keys were used to create admins and install malicious plugins on connected WordPress sites. The fixed UpdraftPlus revokes keys made before Oct 18.
advisories.affected: WordPress sites connected to UpdraftCentral cloud; UpdraftPlus Premium users should check. Self-hosted UpdraftCentral is not affected.
patch: Update UpdraftPlus to 1.26.13 (free) or 2.26.13 (Premium)
Delete the UpdraftCentral key, remove unknown admins and plugins, change admin passwords, re-authorise remote storage, change your teamupdraft.com password
iocs: Admin accounts or plugins you did not create

advisories.title: Strapi: template injection to RCE, now exploited (CISA KEV)
advisories.summary: Two 2023 Strapi bugs chain to unauthenticated code execution on self-hosted instances; CISA added them to its exploited list on Oct 8.
advisories.affected: Strapi 4 before 4.8.0 (CVE-2023-22621: 4.5.5 and older) and every Strapi 3.
patch: npm install @strapi/strapi@latest (4.8.0 or newer; Strapi 5 is current) and rebuild
Strapi 3: migrate, it gets no fix

advisories.title: Nextcloud: command injection in the built-in Collabora server, exploited
advisories.summary: Unauthenticated command injection through proxy.php in the Collabora Online built-in CODE server app (richdocumentscode).
advisories.affected: richdocumentscode before 26.4.303.
patch: sudo -u www-data php occ app:update richdocumentscode (or update it in Apps), or disable the app
mitigation: php occ app:disable richdocumentscode until updated

advisories.title: Plex2Shell: Plex Media Server chain exploited for miners and proxies
advisories.summary: A four-bug chain in Plex Media Server, exploited since Oct 17 to drop crypto miners and proxy malware; CISA added it to its exploited list on Oct 20.
advisories.affected: Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861.
patch: Update Plex Media Server to 1.43.3.10861 or newer (package manager or Plex's download page)
mitigation: Keep Plex off the public internet until updated
iocs: Unknown processes using CPU (miners) under the plex user

advisories.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker carried a credential stealer
advisories.summary: A release built from a lookalike repo put cook.pth in site-packages, so the stealer runs on every Python start. It takes cloud keys, SSH keys, .env files, AI tool configs, and every provider key in the LiteLLM database.
advisories.affected: litellm==1.107.0 from PyPI (all seven wheels, Oct 21 11:39-13:23 UTC); Docker Hub and GHCR (ghcr.io/berriai/litellm, litellm-database, litellm-non_root) tags v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, main-stable pulled Oct 21 11:46-14:20 UTC (GHCR until 13:51 UTC). The GitHub v1.107.0 source tag is clean.

checks.label: cook.pth in site-packages
command: import site,glob,os; d=site.getsitepackages()+[site.getusersitepackages()]; print(chr(10).join(f for x in d for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(x,'cook.p*'))))

patch: Isolate the host; rebuild the virtualenv or image from scratch (do not pip install over it); pin litellm==1.106.2 or a later clean release, and pin Docker images by digest

Rotate everything the host could read: cloud keys and instance roles, SSH/GPG keys, .env files, .npmrc/.pypirc/.git-credentials, kube/docker/gh tokens, AI tool keys, and every provider key stored in LiteLLM's database

advisories.title: OVHcloud CLI releases replaced with a secret stealer
advisories.summary: Release binaries v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 were swapped for a secret stealer through a compromised contributor account, for installs via install.sh, Homebrew or GitHub tarballs on Oct 19 14:47-16:21 UTC.
advisories.affected: ovhcloud-cli v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 installed in that window (Go-module, source and Docker installs are clean).
patch: Update to v0.16.0 or delete the binary
If it was installed in the window: change every secret on that disk

advisories.title: npm: fake Web3 accelerator packages install a stealer and hijack AI agents
advisories.summary: @apexacc/cli and @apexacc/audit drop a Windows stealer or macOS backdoor and reroute AI agent traffic through an attacker's proxy and a persistent MCP server.
advisories.affected: Any project or machine that installed @apexacc/cli or @apexacc/audit.
patch: Remove the packages, check your AI agent configs for an MCP server or model proxy you did not add, rotate keys on that machine
iocs: apexacc in ~/.config or agent config folders

advisories.title: eMudhra CA: weak keys let anyone forge TLS certificates
advisories.summary: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys were generated with weak entropy (one key was the number 4), so certificates for any domain could be forged. Chrome blocked them on Oct 17 and removes the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 on Oct 27.
advisories.affected: Sites whose certificate chains to eMudhra/emSign (they stop working in Chrome on Oct 27); servers, apps and Python environments whose trust store still holds the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 (OS ca-certificates, certifi, pip's and uv's bundled copies, container images).

checks.label: trust store still has emSign ECC Root CA - G3
command: ls /etc/ssl/certs 2>/dev/null | grep -i 'emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_G3' | sed 's|^|system trust store: /etc/ssl/certs/|'; trust list 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'emSign ECC Root CA - G3' && echo 'system trust store: emSign ECC Root CA - G3'; python3 -c "import certifi; p=certifi.where(); print('certifi ' + certifi.__version__ + ': ' + p) if 'emSign ECC Root CA - G3' in open(p).read() else None" 2>/dev/null; true

patch: If your certificate is issued by eMudhra/emSign: get a new one from another CA (e.g. Let's Encrypt: certbot --nginx -d {host}) before Oct 27
Update OS ca-certificates, language runtimes (Node 22.23.4/24.22.1/26.12.1, Go's crypto/x509 fix GO-2026-6809) and bundled trust stores; rebuild images; restart
Python: certifi 2026.10.19, pip 26.2.2, uv 0.13.4, conda 26.9.4 in every virtualenv and tool install (pipx, uv tool); pip and uv carry their own copy, so upgrade them too
Never fix new certificate errors by turning verification off

advisories.title: Railway: customer environment variables accessed
advisories.summary: Railway's environment-variable store was accessed and some values decrypted, in a campaign against platforms hosting AI inference.
advisories.affected: Anyone who deploys on Railway.
patch: Rotate every Railway environment variable, API key, database password and private-registry credential; review service logs

advisories.title: OpenCode Console: linked provider API keys stolen
advisories.summary: 1.4% of OpenCode Console users had their linked external provider keys stolen and abused (rogue charges up to $1,700, Google Cloud projects suspended).
advisories.affected: Anyone who linked provider keys to OpenCode Console.
patch: Revoke and reissue every provider key you linked to OpenCode Console; check provider bills

advisories.title: Zeabur: platform database and clusters breached, shutting down
advisories.summary: Zeabur's shared cluster, dedicated servers and platform database (environment variables) were read; it is its second breach in two months and the service shuts down in December.
advisories.affected: Anyone who deployed on Zeabur.
patch: Replace every password and key stored on Zeabur, even ones rotated in August, and migrate off

advisories.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup OAuth app abused to read Microsoft 365 tenants
advisories.summary: A vendor credential for the SkyKick/ConnectWise Cloud Backup app was used to read mail, files and directory data across Microsoft 365 tenants through Graph.
advisories.affected: Microsoft 365 tenants that granted the ConnectWise Cloud Backup (SkyKick) app.
patch: In Entra ID, disable (not delete) enterprise apps 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae and 24205314-2b89-4e07-a2a4-579e898a5640; review credentials added to all apps

advisories.title: Linux KVM PwnEscape: guest VM can take over the host (CVE-2026-99999)
advisories.summary: Crafted packets from a guest VM leak host memory, crash the host, or run code as root on it. It matters to anyone hosting other people's VMs (VPS providers, sandboxes); a site on a VPS depends on its provider having rebooted into a patched kernel.
advisories.affected: KVM hosts on unpatched kernels.
patch: VM hosts: install the distro's patched kernel and reboot
VPS customers: confirm your provider patched its hosts

advisories.title: Apache Tomcat: 8 fixes including an authentication bypass
advisories.summary: Eight vulnerabilities, including an authentication bypass and an HTTP/2 response mix-up.
advisories.affected: Tomcat 11 before 11.0.27 and 10.1 before 10.1.61.
patch: Upgrade to 11.0.27 or 10.1.61 ($CATALINA_HOME/bin/version.sh shows yours)

advisories.title: SiteGuard Server Edition: local command injection to root, exploited
advisories.summary: The host WAF's statistics feature (on by default) lets a low-privilege local user become root; CISA added it to its exploited list on Oct 20.
advisories.affected: SiteGuard Server Edition 2.20 and later with statistics on.
patch: Apply Ver8.00 Update 5 (Apache/Nginx/IIS) or Ver7.00 Update 6 (FreeBSD), or the vendor's file-replacement patch
mitigation: Turn the statistics feature off until patched
